newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Bunds head for 103.61 on way to 104.00.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Bunds head for 103.61 on way to 104.00.

text.p: September Bund futures traded on LIFFE face resistance from continuation charts at 103.61, after hurdling resistance at the contract high in early trade, technical analysts said on Wednesday.

Bunds opened up 49 basis points at 103.52, following strong gains in U.S. Treasuries overnight. Analysts said that had provided the impetus for Bunds to smash through the contract high of 103.15, a level which had thwarted the market in recent sessions.
"The obvious target now is the 104.00 area," said David Wood, an independent technical analyst based near London.
September Bund futures were up 0.45 at 103.48 by 0715 GMT.
On continuation charts, Bunds set a high of 103.61 in early March 1997.
Above there, Wood said the market was shooting for all-time highs of 104.04 and 103.98 in February 1997.
He said he advised buying the market in the low 103.20s, as the strength of the upmove may curb attempts by the market to fill the gap left down to the July 9 high of 103.15.
"After such a gap up it may not be able to fill that gap fully," he said. "A pullback all the way could be a problem."

Analysts at RBS Futures said in a research note that Bunds were supported by a broken trendline on continuation charts, joining the 104.04 high to the 103.15 high. That line hits the market at 103.07 this session, they said.
Below there, the value area from 102.90 down to 102.50 was expected to act as support.
They advised buying dips, looking for a bull target of 103.75.
At the short end, December Euromarks were up two basis points at 96.67. Analysts said a break of 96.70 would improve the generally weak technical outlook.
